name: Acute Mast Cell Leukemia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Diagnostic Criteria for Mast Cell Leukemia

criteria.description: Bone marrow biopsy showing ≥20% atypical mast cells
Presence of ≥10% mast cells in peripheral blood
Detection of activating KIT mutation (commonly D816V)
Markedly elevated serum tryptase levels (>20 ng/mL)
Evidence of organ dysfunction related to mast cell infiltration (e.g., hepatosplenomegaly, cytopenias)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of ≥20% atypical mast cells in bone marrow and ≥10% mast cells in peripheral blood
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other myeloid neoplasms and confirmation of mast cell lineage.

laboratory: Peripheral blood smear showing ≥10% atypical mast cells
Anemia, thrombocytopenia, and leukocytosis or leukopenia
imaging: Hepatosplenomegaly on abdominal ultrasound or CT
Bone marrow biopsy demonstrating dense mast cell infiltration
other: Flow cytometry showing aberrant mast cell immunophenotype (CD25+, CD2+)
Elevated serum histamine and other mast cell mediators

distinguishingFeatures: Lower percentage of circulating mast cells (<10%)
Presence of myeloblasts with partial mast cell differentiation
Lower mast cell percentage in blood and marrow

redFlags: High peripheral blood mast cell count (>10%)
Signs of organ failure (hepatic, renal, cardiac) due to mast cell infiltration
